_meta.indication: STELARA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients (18 years or older) with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 3 arms during the initial 12-week period: 45 mg ustekinumab, 90 mg ustekinumab, and placebo, with injections at baseline and Week 4
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years and older with plaque-type psoriasis for 6 months or more, baseline PASI score >= 12, psoriasis covering >= 10% total body surface area, candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy; Study 08 enrolled 766 subjects
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint PASI 75 (75% or greater reduction in PASI score) at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: Week 12 PASI 75 response: 171 (67%) with 45 mg and 170 (66%) with 90 mg vs 8 (3%) placebo, p<0.001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 3 arms during the initial 12-week period: 45 mg ustekinumab, 90 mg ustekinumab, and placebo, with injections at baseline and Week 4
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years and older with plaque-type psoriasis for 6 months or more, baseline PASI score >= 12, psoriasis covering >= 10% total body surface area, candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy; Study 09 enrolled 1230 subjects
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint PASI 75 (75% or greater reduction in PASI score) at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: Week 12 PASI 75 response: 273 (67%) with 45 mg and 311 (76%) with 90 mg vs 15 (4%) placebo, p<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >3% and greater than placebo): nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, headache, and fatigue. Serious risks of concern include serious infections and malignancies; one case of reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy syndrome (RPLS) was reported among 3523 STELARA-treated subjects.
target_moa: Ustekinumab is a fully humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds with high affinity to the p40 subunit shared by interleukin (IL)-12 and IL-23, neutralizing their bioactivity and preventing binding to the IL-12RB1 receptor on immune cells.
modality: mAb (fully humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody)

rems.type: A Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) was required, whose elements include a Medication Guide appended to the package insert and provided with each single-unit carton.

advisory_committee.vote: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmologic Drugs Advisory Committee met on June 27, 2008; the committee voted unanimously that efficacy was demonstrated, voted 7-3 for approval of the 45 mg and 90 mg dosing as studied, and voted unanimously for approval without additional premarket studies.

summary.text: STELARA (ustekinumab) is a first-in-class fully humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody against the shared IL-12/IL-23 p40 subunit, approved September 25, 2009 for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis. The BLA was received November 29, 2007; the first-cycle action was a Complete Response on December 18, 2008, and approval followed in a later cycle with a required REMS and multiple postmarketing requirements.

citations.quote: Ustekinumab is a first-in-class new molecular entity proposed for the treatment of plaque psoriasis.
